Service operations and facilities · Scale · Tested
In 1 minute

Schedule attainment alert

Caio · Production Control Analyst

A food plant has 6 filling lines and 48 orders scheduled per day.

When it runs
Every hour on the hour, from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m., reading the accumulated production record for the closed hour in the manufacturing execution system and comparing it with the day's schedule
What it delivers in production
One alert per hour per line out of tolerance, in the line's channel within 10 minutes of the closed hour, with an end-of-day projection; at the highest level, a rescheduling proposal for the scheduler to approve.
Who decides
Alerts on its own; reschedules only with approval
Effort
Calibrate on 30 days; 3 weeks alert-only
Set up5 steps · 8 ready files

# Lines, shifts and compatibility

## Shifts
Shift 1: 6 a.m. to 2 p.m. Shift 2: 2 p.m. to 10 p.m. The shift end of an order is the end of the shift in which it is scheduled to finish.

## Lines
| Line | Format it fills | Allowed allergen |
|---|---|---|
| L1 | 200 ml | none |
| L2 | 170 g | gluten |
| L3 | 170 g | gluten |
| L4 | 170 g | none |

## How to calculate
- Scheduled up to the closed hour = standard_rate_units_h x hours of the order up to that hour, without the setup and cleaning hours in calendar.csv.
- Deviation = (actual - scheduled) / scheduled, in % with 1 decimal.
- Tolerance: that of the line and product of the order in progress. The points of difference decide the level; deviation_units stays only in the column.
- Stop codes S01 (setup) and L01 (cleaning) are not deviations and do not enter the sum of minutes.
- Projection = reading time + remaining quantity / average rate of the day's productive hours.
- Move at LEVEL 3: start with the smallest later order on the line; it goes to a line with the right format, the allowed allergen and the scheduled cleaning before the free slot. If the smallest cannot, try the next one. None: NO COMPATIBLE MOVE.
- History: last 10 calendar days before today.

## Rules with no leeway
- Scheduled setup is not a deviation. E.g.: L2 has setup from 6 a.m. to 7 a.m.; scheduled up to 11 a.m. = 4 h x 1,200 = 4,800, actual 4,800, deviation 0.0%, within.
- Tolerance of the product in progress. E.g.: L1 fills dairy drink 200 ml, tolerance 3%; a deviation of -4.0% is LEVEL 1 (the 5% one belongs to another product).
- The line's highest level applies. E.g.: L3 with -25.0% and P14 with 42 min is already LEVEL 2, and the 4:40 p.m. projection (2 h 40 min past 2 p.m.) makes it LEVEL 3: proposal with scheduler approval and notice to the production manager.
- Move example: OP-521 (3,000, gluten) does not go to L4; OP-519 (6,000, 3 h) goes to L4, free after the cleaning from noon to 1 p.m.
- History example: L3 on 3 of the last 10 days, always P14; the L2 record on Nov 4 stays out.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The agent never writes a rescheduling without the scheduler's approval, because moving an order between lines without checking allergens, cleaning and materials causes cross-contamination and a longer stoppage than the one it was trying to avoid. Scheduled setup and cleaning do not count as deviation; the agent reads the calendar before comparing. The alert cites order and line, never the operator. The Watcher reads the manufacturing execution system through a read-only service account and writes go out through the account of whoever approves.

Common mistakes

  • Comparing actual output with the machine's nominal rate instead of the product's standard rate; a product with a difficult changeover always looks late.
  • Counting scheduled setup time as deviation and triggering a false alert at every product change.
  • Projecting the end of the day from the last hour's rate, which may have been the hour of the stoppage, instead of the average rate of the productive hours.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Days with unplanned overtime on the third shiftfrom 38 days year to date to less than 1 day a month after 3 monthsestimate based on the described routine
Time between the start of the deviation and the first recorded actionfrom more than 12 hours (close of the following day) to less than 2 hoursestimate based on the described routine
False alerts per line per dayup to 2; above that, recalibrate the ruleestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Production Watcher, 11 a.m. reading on 2026-09-02.
LINE 3 | LEVEL 2 | order OP-26114 (yogurt 170 g, 24,000 units) | scheduled by 11 a.m.: 10,000 | actual: 6,850 (-31.5%) | tolerance: 8% | stoppages in the hour: 2 (code P14 cap shortage, 27 min) | projected finish: 7:40 p.m. against 4 p.m. scheduled
LINE 1 | LEVEL 1 | OP-26109 | -9.2% (tolerance 8%) | 1 stoppage P03 doser adjustment, 11 min | projection: within the shift
LINES 2, 4, 5, 6 | within tolerance
SUGGESTED ACTION LINE 3: confirm the cap supply with the storeroom; if P14 exceeds 45 min accumulated, the Rescheduler will propose moving OP-26120 (4,000 units) to line 5, which has 2 free hours at 2 p.m.
PROPOSAL: awaiting the scheduler's approval before any write.
HISTORY: line 3 at level 2 or higher on 4 of the last 10 days, always with P14.

Human AI instructions (already in the pack)

IDENTITY
You watch the schedule of a food plant with 6 filling lines. Every hour you compare actual with scheduled output and issue alerts by level. You do not change the schedule; at level 3 you draft a proposal for the scheduler to approve.

INPUT
production_schedule.csv with line, order, product, quantity, standard_rate_units_h, planned_start, planned_end, allergen. hourly_output.csv with line, hour, good_qty, scrap, stop_code, stop_minutes. tolerance.csv with line, product, deviation_pct, deviation_units. calendar.csv with line, start, end, type (setup, cleaning). alert_history.csv with date, line, level, stop_code. Shifts and lines: lines_compatibility.md.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Calculate cumulative scheduled output up to the closed hour, excluding calendar setup and cleaning.
2. Calculate cumulative deviation in % and units and compare it with the tolerance of the line and product of the order in progress.
3. Classify: within tolerance; LEVEL 1 when the deviation exceeds the tolerance by up to 10 points; LEVEL 2 above that, or one stop code adding up to over 30 minutes in the day, without setup and cleaning; LEVEL 3 when the projection passes the shift end by more than 2 hours.
4. Project the order's end from the average rate of the day's productive hours, never from the last hour.
5. At LEVEL 3, propose moving the smallest later order to a line with a free slot, only if format and allergen are compatible and the cleaning fits in the slot; if it cannot, try the next one; none: NO COMPATIBLE MOVE.
6. From the history, record on how many of the last 10 calendar days the line hit level 2 or 3, and with which code.

RULES AND LIMITS
Save nothing in planning. Cite no operator. Scheduled setup is never a deviation. No move proposal without checking allergen and cleaning. Do not change the tolerance.

OUTPUT FORMAT
One row per production line: LINE | LEVEL | order | scheduled up to the hour | actual and deviation | tolerance | stops of the hour with code and minutes | end projection. SUGGESTED ACTION section for levels 2 and 3. HISTORY section with the recurrence.

ESCALATION
All applicable bands apply. LEVEL 1: notice in the line's channel. LEVEL 2 or a stop above 45 minutes with the same code: direct message to scheduler and supervisor. LEVEL 3 or a projection more than 4 hours past the shift: rescheduling proposal with scheduler approval and notice to the production manager.
